stem.text: Let \( W(t) = \int_{0}^{t} \left(3 e^{\frac{s}{3}} + 3\right)\,ds \) for \( 0 \le t \le 7 \). Using a calculator, find the value of t in the interval \( 1 < t < 3 \) at which the instantaneous rate of change of W equals the average rate of change of W over \( 1 \le t \le 3 \). Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The average rate of change of W over the interval is \( \frac{W(3) - W(1)}{3 - 1} = \frac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{3} \left(3 e^{\frac{s}{3}} + 3\right)\,ds \), which a calculator gives as about 8.952 (more places are kept).
By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, \( W'(t) = 3 e^{\frac{t}{3}} + 3 \). Set \( W'(t) \) equal to the average rate of change and solve on \( 1 < t < 3 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: instantaneous rate set equal to the average rate

worked_solution.text: The calculator's solver gives one solution in the interval, \( t = 2.055 \).

options.derivation: the average rate of change rounded to one decimal place before solving
W at both endpoints rounded to whole numbers before forming the average rate of change
the average rate of change taken over 0 to 3 instead of the stated interval, then solved on that wider interval
